official.deadline_central_display: 1 November 2026 (Early Decision I and Early Action, Fall 2027 entry)
official.deadline_note: The scholarship deadline is the admission-plan application deadline, not a separate scholarship date. Early Decision I and Early Action both close 1 November 2026; their financial aid deadline is 15 November 2026 and final credentials deadlines are 13 November (EDI) and 20 November (EA). Applications still incomplete at the final credentials deadline are rolled into Regular Decision, which is considered for merit scholarships only and therefore loses Stamps consideration.
official.status_note: The University of Miami has published its Fall 2027 first-year admission plans and deadlines; Early Decision I and Early Action both close 1 November 2026 and are the only plans considered for premier scholarships.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Stamps Scholarship includes tuition and fees, on-campus housing, a meal plan, University health insurance, textbooks, a laptop allowance, and access to a $12,000 enrichment fund; scholars receive the full cost of attendance for eight semesters (10 semesters for students in five-year degree programs) or the completion of the first degree, whichever is sooner.
benefits: Full cost of attendance for eight semesters (10 semesters for students in five-year degree programs) or the completion of the first degree, whichever is sooner.
Tuition and fees, on-campus housing, a meal plan, University health insurance, textbooks, and a laptop allowance.
Access to a $12,000 enrichment fund; enrichment fund expenses are subject to prior approval and may support study abroad, undergraduate research, unpaid internships, and other educational pursuits.
Exclusive programs, one-on-one advising, group community service efforts, and personal referrals for additional prestigious academic opportunities through the Office of Academic Enhancement.
eligibility: Apply and be admitted through either the Early Decision I or Early Action admission plans.
There is no separate application outside of the Common Application to be considered.
Exceptional academic achievement, leadership, and curiosity.
Selected through the University of Miami's holistic review process.
requirements: Complete a full-time undergraduate program of study with no fewer than 12 credit hours during each of the fall and spring semesters, for a minimum of 24 credit hours per academic year.
Maintain a minimum 3.0 GPA for the academic year at the University of Miami, with the initial calculation at the end of the second semester of attendance.
The award is subject to revision pending receipt of any grant, scholarship, or prepaid tuition and/or housing aid not anticipated at the time the award is made.
Enrichment fund expenses are subject to prior approval.
documents: Common Application, including the $75 nonrefundable application fee.
One letter of recommendation/evaluation from a school counselor or teacher.

School Report and official high school/secondary school transcripts; if not in English, a translation issued by a school official or an accredited translation agency (self-translated transcripts are unofficial and cannot be used).
SAT or ACT scores, self-reported on the Common Application or Applicant Portal; official reports only required if admitted and enrolling.
Official TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test results for applicants whose native language is not English, unless waived.
CSS Profile, required of international students to be considered for institutional need-based aid.
selection_criteria: Semi-finalist interview with the Stamps Scholarship Committee, conducted by mid-January.
Finalist interview with the Stamps Foundation.
Finalists are notified of their status at the Early Action decision release in late January.
coverage: Full cost of attendance for eight semesters (10 for five-year degree programs) or completion of the first degree, whichever is sooner.
On-campus housing and a meal plan.
A $12,000 enrichment fund for study abroad, undergraduate research, unpaid internships, and other educational pursuits.
application_method: Submit the Common Application under Early Decision I or Early Action; there is no separate Stamps scholarship application.
All applicants are automatically considered for merit scholarships when they apply for admission to the University of Miami.
official.application_route: Common Application under Early Decision I or Early Action by 1 November 2026 - no separate scholarship application, Stamps consideration is automatic with the admission application.
official.study_mode: Full-time (no fewer than 12 credit hours in each of the fall and spring semesters)
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship or residency restriction is published; consideration depends on the admission plan rather than nationality, and the University's published award figures cover both domestic and international students.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - no nationality restriction is published. UM publishes a separate international-student cost of attendance of $104,091 that includes the mandatory University health insurance the award covers, international students appear on the official Stamps Scholars roster, and international applicants must meet UM's English proficiency requirement and submit the CSS Profile for need-based aid consideration.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: None published; open to any field of study across the University of Miami's schools and colleges.
official.duration: Eight semesters, or 10 semesters for students in five-year degree programs, or until completion of the first degree, whichever is sooner.
official.description: The Stamps Scholarship is the University of Miami's most prestigious merit award, recognizing exceptional students whose academic achievement, leadership, and curiosity position them to make the most of a University of Miami education. Stamps Scholars receive the full cost of attendance for eight semesters, or 10 semesters for students in five-year degree programs, or until completion of their first degree, whichever is sooner.
official.program_type: Merit-based premier scholarship - the University of Miami's most prestigious merit award
official.english_requirement: Applicants whose native language is not English must submit official TOEFL (internet-based, Home Edition accepted, Essentials not accepted), IELTS, or Duolingo English Test results, sent directly from the testing agency, unless waived. Competitive applicants generally score above TOEFL 80 on the 0-120 scale (before 21 January 2026) or 4.5 on the 1-6 scale (after 21 January 2026), IELTS 6.5, or DET 120; scores are valid for two years. Waivers include an A or B in AP/HL IB English, three years at an English-medium high school (including in the United States), Level 5 of UM's Intensive English Program, IGCSE/GCE O or A Level English as a first language with a grade of C or better, a verified SAT evidence-based reading and writing score of 650 or higher, an ACT English score of 27 or higher, or 24 or more US post-secondary credits including 6 English Composition credits graded B or higher.

not_confirmed: The University of Miami publishes no fixed dollar stipend or per-award amount for the Stamps Scholarship; the recorded figure is its published 2026-2027 estimated total cost of attendance for on-campus undergraduates ($98,872 domestic / $104,091 international), which is what the award covers.
Number of Stamps Scholarships awarded per cycle and any minimum test-score or GPA threshold for selection are not published; selection is described as holistic with no published cut-offs.

Travel is not itemised in the scholarship's own benefit list; travel_coverage is recorded as true because the award is stated to be the full cost of attendance, which the University defines to include a transportation allowance.
The exact mid-January, late-January, and early-March interview and announcement dates are given only as timeframes, not calendar dates.

applicant_utility.summary: The only door into this award is Early Decision I or Early Action for Fall 2027, with a 1 November 2026 deadline - Early Decision II and Regular Decision applicants are considered for merit scholarships only, so a January application effectively forfeits Stamps. There is no separate scholarship application: your Common Application is the scholarship application, semi-finalists interview with the Stamps Scholarship Committee by mid-January, finalists are told at the Early Action release in late January and then interview with the Stamps Foundation, and recipients are announced in early March. Plan for the gap between the University's published $98,872 on-campus cost and what actually lands on your bill, and remember that outside scholarships or grants you did not disclose can trigger a revision of the award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-of-class students with a demonstrated leadership and impact story who can commit to the University of Miami by 1 November and want a debt-free four-year experience.
application_readiness_checklist: Decide by late October whether you can sign the binding Early Decision Agreement; if not, apply non-binding Early Action, which carries identical Stamps consideration with the same 1 November date.

Get the counselor/teacher letter, School Report and official transcripts into the Common App before the final credentials deadlines of 13 November (EDI) and 20 November (EA), because an incomplete early file is rolled into Regular Decision and loses Stamps consideration.
Sit the TOEFL, IELTS, or DET no later than October: UM warns that November results may not arrive in time for the Early Decision I / Early Action review, and scores older than two years are invalid.
File the CSS Profile by 15 November if you want any need-based aid - it is mandatory for international students seeking institutional need-based aid.
Build two interview-ready narratives (leadership and curiosity) plus a concrete, approvable plan for the $12,000 enrichment fund, since both interviews happen within about eight weeks of submission.
common_rejection_risks: Applying Early Decision II or Regular Decision: those plans are considered for merit scholarships only, so the file never reaches the Stamps committee.
Missing the final credentials date (13 November EDI / 20 November EA), which rolls an early application into Regular Decision and silently removes it from Stamps review.
A generic high-achiever file: UM's review is explicitly holistic and the award is built on leadership and curiosity, so grades alone will not carry it.
Unofficial or self-prepared documents, especially self-translated transcripts, which UM treats as unofficial and cannot use in the admission process.
English test timing - a November sitting can miss committee consideration, and a score more than two years old has to be retaken.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything above the published cost of attendance is on you: flights beyond the transportation allowance, personal spending above the $2,294 allowance, dependent or specialised health coverage, and summer-term costs, since renewal is tied to fall and spring full-time enrollment. Outside scholarships must be reported to the financial aid office, because total aid cannot exceed the cost of attendance and the Stamps award is subject to revision when unanticipated grants, scholarships, or prepaid tuition or housing aid arrive.
document_audit: Transcript translations must be issued by a school official or an accredited agency and sent in original form via the Common Application, Slate.org, SCOIR, Parchment, or mydocuments@miami.edu; photocopies, screenshots, and self-translations are rejected.
Only one letter of recommendation is required, from a counselor or a teacher - additional letters are not part of the file UM reviews.
Use one email address across the whole process (a personal address is recommended), and note that the Applicant Portal only opens from mid-September.
A gap of three months or more between secondary graduation and your entry term requires an Educational Activities statement in the Common Application before the file is complete.
No supplemental essay is required, so the Common App personal statement of 650 words or less is the main writing sample the holistic review sees.
alerts: The 1 November 2026 deadline is the admission-plan application deadline, and it is the only Stamps deadline - there is no separate scholarship submission and no later consideration.
Early Decision I is binding and requires the Early Decision Agreement form in the Common Application; use non-binding Early Action if you are not ready to commit.
Keep January and February clear: finalists are notified at the Early Action decision release in late January and then interview with the Stamps Foundation, with recipients announced in early March.
Renewal depends on staying full-time (at least 12 credits each fall and spring, 24 per year) and holding a 3.0 GPA, first measured at the end of your second semester.
The Frost School of Music Stamps Ensemble Scholarship is a separate award with its own application requirements - do not confuse it with this scholarship.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the Common Application under Early Decision I or Early Action by 1 November 2026, with credentials finalised by 13 or 20 November, then automatic merit and premier-scholarship review, a semi-finalist interview with the Stamps Scholarship Committee by mid-January, finalist notification at the Early Action release in late January, an interview with the Stamps Foundation, and recipient announcements in early March.
